records.supported_name_scope: Paalliq is directly and repeatedly printed along the eastern lower river, its lake-like widenings, and its approach to Byron Bay. Fisheries and Oceans Canada associates this river with Lauchlan River and the local spelling Paalik; the Inuinnaqtun version prints Paalliq. These are source-attributed spellings, not a formal naming-date or preferred-spelling adjudication.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The route lies west of the Wellington Bay fisheries and extends far inland northwest of Byron Bay. The opening crosses a lobed western lake complex before a northeastward reversal into smaller eastern lakes; farther southeast it passes broad unnamed lakes and a north-south channel corridor before entering the elongated east-west lake country upstream of Paalliq. The named lower river trends east and southeast to the northwestern shore of Byron Bay. The identification is tied to the actual lower channel and receiving bay, rather than proximity to a regional name.
records.region: South-central Victoria Island, Nunavut, Canada, from northwestern interior lake country through the Paalliq/Lauchlan corridor to Byron Bay.
records.completion_scope: All of the single retained feature and its 57 constituent sublines received geographic coverage in five successful original federal raster views. Original northwest, middle and southeast pixels, the focused northwest connector, and necessary local original crops were inspected alongside separate orientation copies. Complete geographic coverage has not established the required northwest lake-to-lake passage. The independent fisheries thesis corroborates the regional basin and lower outlet, but does not resolve that passage.
records.material_pending_reason: At the northwest reversal, the selection leaves the southern arm of the larger western lake complex and passes northeast through a separate small-lake sequence before turning east. Detailed original cartography shows intervening contoured ridge/land intervals, separate lake margins, and channels taking other routes; a continuous aquatic connector following this selected component sequence was not established. A general basin association or the well-supported downstream name cannot supply that missing connection. This is not a claim that every modeled vertex must coincide with the source, that the geometry is proved wrong, or that no connection can exist.

records.supported_name_scope: Río Imperial is the representative downstream system identity; distinct component names are retained and no full-river or full-basin extent is inferred.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The modeled mainstem follows Quino and Colpi/Pangueco into Cholchol, rather than selecting Traiguén, northern Lumaco or Quillén as its opening. The long eastern branch follows Cautín; the southern branch is lower Quepe. The terminal is Imperial water east of the Moncul confluence, not Moncul, Lago Budi, Laguna Trovolhue or the Pacific outlet.
records.region: Araucanía, Chile: Quino–Colpi/Cholchol and Cautín–Quepe corridors to the lower Imperial estuary at Nehuentúe.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported representative identity of the complete seven-feature connected selection; not a scalar name for Quino, Colpi/Pangueco, Cholchol, Cautín or Quepe.
records.completion_scope: All seven complete cached paths reviewed against independent original source renderings, including three mainstem and four tributary features, initial corridors, joining settings and the exact selected estuarine terminal. This is generalized corridor correspondence, not pointwise fitting, source-vector comparison, geometry revalidation, a current hydrological survey or precision assignment of every name transition.

records.supported_name_scope: Ochlockonee River is the representative identity of the complete selected connected corridor. Lake Talquin is the named reservoir traversed within that system; the terminal receiving water is Ochlockonee Bay. This does not assign the river hydronym to the whole reservoir or bay, or to neighboring tributaries.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Direct original cartography was read in geographic order over the entire feature. The opening takes Ochlockonee River itself, not either separate Little Ochlockonee River. The line stays west of Lakes Iamonia and Jackson, crosses Talquin from its eastern river arm rather than the northern Little River arm, reaches the lower turn from Jackson Bluff rather than Telogia Creek, and remains on the main Ochlockonee tidal outlet rather than turning into Crooked River or using the Sopchoppy mouth. The endpoint is at western Ochlockonee Bay, not the open Gulf.
records.region: Southwestern Georgia and the Florida Panhandle, United States: Worth and Colquitt counties through the Thomas-Grady corridor, Lake Talquin and the lower Ochlockonee to western Ochlockonee Bay.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported representative river-system identity for the entire selected mainstem, with its Lake Talquin crossing and terminal estuarine setting kept explicit.
records.completion_scope: All 63 constituent sublines of feature 9987 were inspected against three overlapping original national raster views, their original local enlargements and separately marked orientation copies. Those views cover every selected interval, headward junction, reservoir crossing, middle reach and final estuarine branch. Independent Georgia and Florida plans provide bounded descriptive corroboration. No material route connection or branch remains unresolved; ordinary generalized meanders and exact river-to-reservoir or river-to-bay label boundaries are not treated as gaps.

records.supported_name_scope: Original federal cartography repeatedly labels Lorillard River along the southbound and eastbound trunk, the long middle valley and the final eastward outlet reach. Its separately mapped northwest headward branch is distinguished from the selected northern feeder. The complete selection is a connected feeder-to-Lorillard route, not evidence of one uniform hydronym along every constituent subline.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected opening occupies small lake-and-stream country west of a larger eastern lake, enters their common southbound channel, turns southwest to the northwest Lorillard branch, continues south and then east through broad rapids-and-island reaches, and turns into the long southeastward valley east of Hazard Hills. The lower route turns west, crosses a broad lake-like river reach southward, and bends east into the coastal outlet complex. The distinct Connery River and Smoke Lake setting southwest of the outlet is not selected as a continuation.
records.region: Kivalliq, Nunavut, Canada: the lake country south of Wager Bay, the Lorillard River corridor east of Hazard Hills, and the Daly Bay coastal setting.
records.completion_scope: All of the single retained feature and its 48 constituent sublines were read against six successful original national raster views: complete corridor, upper, middle, lower, detailed opening and detailed terminal. The actual lake/stream relationships, joining branches, long trunk and coastal outlet setting are established at generalized component scale. There is no unresolved material branch or connector. Straight lake passages, island and bank shortcuts, and exact hydronym or estuary-transition limits are ordinary model/name-scope limitations, not unresolved correspondence.
